title: Bulk report - Week 46
summary:
Capesize
The Capesize market maintained a positive trajectory throughout the week, with the Pacific emerging as the clear driver of overall gains. Despite some midweek volatility, improving miner demand and increasingly competitive fixing levels saw C5 recover strongly, climbing from $13.80 on Monday to $15.20 by Thursday, before easing back to $14.50-$14.60 towards the end of the week. Activity picked up considerably, particularly from Wednesday onwards, with both Port Hedland and Dampier miners covering multiple cargoes and operators increasingly willing to pay into the low-mid $15s.

children.title: Panamax-Kamsarmax
children.summary: The market delivered contrasting performances this week, with the Atlantic maintaining a firm tone while the Pacific struggled to gain momentum. Strong transatlantic demand and limited prompt tonnage supported rates, with an 82,000-dwt fixing around $18,000 for a US East Coast round trip and another at $22,250 basis South Africa for an East Coast South America transatlantic trip.

children.title: Ultramax/Supramax
children.summary: After declining for two weeks, the 11TC average showed positive returns in the second half of the week due to an improving Atlantic market. The North American market saw extremely limited tonnage for November dates, with transatlantic rates flying to new highs as a 63,000-dwt fixed for grains US Gulf to Continent/Mediterranean at $39,000 and a 64,000-dwt fixed for similar business at $40,000.

children.title: Handysize
children.summary: The week completed on a steady-to-firmer note, with sentiment largely positional across both basins. Across the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained limited, although rates began to show signs of firmness towards the end of the week.
